Jerusalem sits lonely like a widow. How does the Bible give words for deep grief?
"Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by?" How can you notice those who suffer?
"My eyes flow with tears; for a comforter is far from me." Who needs comfort around you?
The poet confesses and cries out to God. How can confession and lament go together?
The poet's eyes were spent with weeping for the children. What breaks your heart?
"Pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord." What do you need to pour out to God?
The poet describes deep affliction and loss of hope. When have you felt like this?
"The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning." How have you seen God's new mercies?
"The Lord is my portion... It is good that one should wait quietly for the salvation of the Lord." What are you waiting for?
"He does not afflict from his heart." What does this show about God's heart in hard times?
"Let us test and examine our ways, and return to the Lord!" What would returning to the Lord look like for you?
The poet describes terrible suffering in the city. How does honesty about suffering help us?
"The punishment of your iniquity, O daughter of Zion, is accomplished." What hope is there after judgement?
"Remember, O Lord, what has befallen us." What do you need God to remember?
"You, O Lord, reign forever... Restore us to yourself, O Lord, that we may be restored!" Where do you need God's restoring?
